cases.summary: The rider was charged for a materially longer route: actual 9678 m vs reference 7956 m, an excess of 1722 m (+21.6%), exceeding the RD-1 materiality threshold of 796 m. The fare of S$13.16 was computed on the longer distance. However, the record contains a documented navigation reroute (GPS-NAV-01) and a traffic advisory (GPS-ADV-01) for a road closure due to an accident, and the driver notified the rider in chat (CHAT-01), which the rider acknowledged (CHAT-02). Under RD-4, a documented road closure or navigation reroute explains the longer route and no refund is due. The rider's position is therefore weakened by strong counterevidence, and the appropriate outcome is keep_charge.

cases.summary: The GPS trace shows a material detour (+1722 m, +21.6%, exceeding the RD-1 threshold of 796 m), but the excess is fully explained by a documented road closure and navigation reroute, so no refund is due under RD-4. A traffic advisory (ADV-SYN-0412) issued at 13:50:00Z reported a southbound road closure due to an accident between the reference route's second and third waypoints; the navigation system rerouted at 14:03:32Z for road_closure; and the driver notified the rider in chat at 14:03:47Z. The rider replied 'Oh ok.' (tagged agreement) and raised no objection. The fare arithmetic is valid and the driver's conduct was transparent and consistent with the documented diversion.

arguments.claim: A documented road closure and navigation reroute explain the longer route, so no refund is due under RD-4.
The driver proactively informed the rider of the closure and reroute, and the rider acknowledged without objection.
The fare charged is arithmetically valid and matches the actual route distance and duration; there is no billing error.
The detour is material under RD-1, which is the predicate for any excess-distance refund; however RD-4 removes the refund obligation.

counterevidence.claim: The actual route exceeded the reference route by 1722 m (+21.6%), above the RD-1 materiality threshold, which would ordinarily trigger a route-excess refund under RD-2.
The rider's 'Oh ok.' is a brief acknowledgment, not an express approval of a longer route, so RD-3 does not independently bar a refund; the driver's defense rests on RD-4 instead.

missingFacts: Whether the navigation reroute was the only reasonable path or whether an equally short alternative existed.
The exact location and duration of the road closure relative to the trip timeline.
Whether the rider was shown an updated fare estimate at the time of reroute.
Any independent confirmation of the accident/closure beyond the synthetic advisory feed.

retrievedPolicies.ruleText: DEMONSTRATION POLICY. A detour is material when the actual route distance exceeds the reference route distance by more than the greater of 500 metres or 10% of the reference distance.
retrievedPolicies.remedyCriteria: Definition used by RD-2 and RD-5; no remedy on its own.

retrievedPolicies.ruleText: DEMONSTRATION POLICY. When a detour is material under RD-1 and neither RD-3 nor RD-4 applies, refund the eligible excess-distance charge: excess metres x per-kilometre rate x surge multiplier, capped at the surged distance charge and at the amount paid. The server computes the amount.
retrievedPolicies.remedyCriteria: refund_route_excess when RD-1 is met and neither RD-3 nor RD-4 applies.

retrievedPolicies.ruleText: DEMONSTRATION POLICY. No refund is due when the rider requested or expressly approved the longer route before or during the trip.
retrievedPolicies.remedyCriteria: keep_charge when the rider requested or approved the longer route.

retrievedPolicies.ruleText: DEMONSTRATION POLICY. No refund is due when a documented road closure, navigation reroute or equivalent diversion explains the longer route.
retrievedPolicies.remedyCriteria: keep_charge when a documented diversion explains the longer route.

retrievedPolicies.ruleText: DEMONSTRATION POLICY. No refund is due for a deviation that is not material under RD-1.
retrievedPolicies.remedyCriteria: keep_charge when RD-1 is not met.

findings.claim: The actual route exceeded the reference route by 1722 m (+21.6%), which is material under RD-1 (threshold 796 m).
A documented navigation reroute for a road closure explains the longer route, so no refund is due under RD-4.

The driver notified the rider of the closure and reroute in chat, and the rider acknowledged without objection; the chat shows no rider route request or express approval, so RD-3 does not independently apply.
The fare of S$13.16 is arithmetically valid and matches the actual route distance and duration; no billing error.

result.reasoning: GPS-ROUTE shows the RD-1 materiality threshold is exceeded (+1722 m, +21.6% vs 796 m threshold), which would ordinarily trigger a route-excess refund under RD-2. However, RD-4 provides that no refund is due when a documented road closure or navigation reroute explains the longer route. GPS-ADV-01 documents a road closure due to an accident, and GPS-NAV-01 documents the navigation reroute for road_closure at 14:03:32Z, matching the driver's chat message at 14:03:47Z (CHAT-01). The rider acknowledged with 'Oh ok.' (CHAT-02) and raised no objection (CHAT-SUMMARY). Because a documented diversion explains the longer route, RD-4 applies and the charge is kept. RD-3 is not needed as an independent basis since the rider's brief acknowledgement is not an express approval of a longer route. Party history and risk signals are context only and were not used to establish fault (RD-7).
result.riderExplanation: We reviewed your trip and confirmed the route was longer than the app's reference route by about 1.7 km, which is a material detour. However, the records show a documented road closure due to an accident and a navigation reroute at the time of your trip, and the driver messaged you about it. Under our policy, when a documented road closure or reroute explains the longer route, no refund is due. Your fare was also calculated correctly for the distance and time traveled. For these reasons, the charge stands.
